# soft_ratatui - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/soft_ratatui/^0.2.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ratatui-software-backend)Ratatui Software Backend

A collection of software rendering backends for [Ratatui](https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui) that turn
terminal UIs into RGB pixmaps. Perfect for embedding Ratatui into game engines, GUIs, or wherever else.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- **Multiple Font Backends**: Choose from various font rendering technologies
- **Flexible Output**: Get raw RGB data or RGBA with color-to-alpha support
- **Real-time Updates**: Efficient redrawing, perfect for video games
- **Ratatui Compatible**: Full implementation of Ratatui’s- `Backend`trait
- **Bevy Examples**: Show you how to get started with the great game engine, also check out- [bevy_ratatui](https://github.com/cxreiff/bevy_ratatui)

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

- `unicodefonts`- [unicodefonts](https://github.com/j-g00da/embedded-graphics-unicodefonts)(automatically activates- [embedded-graphics](https://github.com/embedded-graphics/embedded-graphics), is the default feature)
- `bdf-parser`- `Bdf`- [bdf-parser](https://github.com/embedded-graphics/bdf))
- `embedded-ttf`- `EmbeddedTTF`- [embedded-graphics](https://github.com/embedded-graphics/embedded-graphics)) (- [embedded-ttf](https://github.com/peckpeck/embedded-ttf))
- `cosmic-text`- `CosmicText`- [cosmic-text](https://github.com/pop-os/cosmic-text))
- `embedded-graphics`- `EmbeddedGraphics`

[§](https://docs.rs#performance)Performance

Generally faster than running ratatui in a terminal with crossterm. Expect hundreds of fps on a normal workload.

[§](https://docs.rs#available-backends)Available Backends

| Backend | Feature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `EmbeddedGraphics` | `embedded-graphics` | Uses embedded-graphics font atlases |
| `EmbeddedTTF` | `embedded-ttf` | TrueType font rendering via RustType |
| `Bdf` | `bdf-parser` | Bitmap Distribution Format fonts |
| `CosmicText` | `cosmic-text` | Advanced text shaping and layout |

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
cargo add soft_ratatui
cargo add ratatui
```
[§](https://docs.rs#minimal-example)Minimal Example

```
use soft_ratatui::embedded_graphics_unicodefonts::{
    mono_8x13_atlas, mono_8x13_bold_atlas, mono_8x13_italic_atlas,
};
use ratatui::Terminal;
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, Borders, Paragraph, Wrap};
use soft_ratatui::{EmbeddedGraphics, SoftBackend};
fn main() {
    let font_regular = mono_8x13_atlas();
    let font_italic = mono_8x13_italic_atlas();
    let font_bold = mono_8x13_bold_atlas();
    let backend = SoftBackend::<EmbeddedGraphics>::new(
        100,
        50,
        font_regular,
        Some(font_bold),
        Some(font_italic),
    );
    let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend).unwrap();
    terminal.clear();
    let _ = terminal.draw(|frame| {
        let area = frame.area();
        let textik = format!("Hello soft! The window area is {}", area);
        frame.render_widget(
            Paragraph::new(textik)
                .block(Block::new().title("Ratatui").borders(Borders::ALL))
                .wrap(Wrap { trim: false }),
            area,
        );
    });
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#usage-patterns)Usage Patterns

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-rendered-output)Getting Rendered Output

```
// Get raw RGB data (3 bytes per pixel: R, G, B)
let rgb_data = backend.get_pixmap_data();
// Get RGBA data (4 bytes per pixel: R, G, B, A)
let rgba_data = backend.get_pixmap_data_as_rgba();
// Get RGBA data with one of the colors set to fully transparent
let transparent_rgba =
    backend.rgb_pixmap.to_rgba_with_color_as_transparent(&(255, 0, 255));
// Get dimensions
let width = backend.get_pixmap_width();
let height = backend.get_pixmap_height();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

See the `examples/` directory for complete working examples with different
backends and font configurations.

[§](https://docs.rs#license)License

This project is licensed under the MIT and Apache2.0 license.

- `pub use`- [embedded_ttf](https://docs.rs/embedded-ttf/0.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/embedded_ttf/index.html);- `embedded-ttf`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bdf](https://docs.rs/struct.Bdf.html)- `bdf-parser`
- Raster backend for bitmap fonts parsed from BDF data.
- [Blink](https://docs.rs/struct.BlinkConfig.html)- Config
- Blink configuration for text modifiers and cursor.
- [Blink](https://docs.rs/struct.BlinkTiming.html)- Timing
- Timing parameters for a single blink pattern.

- [Cursor](https://docs.rs/struct.CursorConfig.html)- Config
- Cursor appearance and blink behavior.
- [Embedded](https://docs.rs/struct.EmbeddedGraphics.html)- Graphics - `embedded-graphics`
- Raster backend built on `embedded-graphics`mono fonts.
- [EmbeddedTTF](https://docs.rs/struct.EmbeddedTTF.html)- `embedded-ttf`
- Raster backend built on `embedded-ttf`and`rusttype`.
- [RgbPixmap](https://docs.rs/struct.RgbPixmap.html)
- An RGB pixmap backed by a flat byte buffer.
- [Soft](https://docs.rs/struct.SoftBackend.html)- Backend

[221](#221)    texture: Option<Res<CuBevyMonTexture>>,
[222](#222)    mut images: ResMut<Assets<Image>>,
[223](#223)) {
[224](#224)    let Some(texture) = texture else {
[225](#225)        return;
[226](#226)    };
[227](#227)
[228](#228)    let width = context.backend().get_pixmap_width() as u32;
[229](#229)    let height = context.backend().get_pixmap_height() as u32;
[230](#230)    let Some(mut image) = images.get_mut(&texture.0) else {
[231](#231)        return;
[232](#232)    };
[233](#233)
[234](#234)    if image.width() != width || image.height() != height {
[235](#235)        image.resize(Extent3d {
[236](#236)            width,
[237](#237)            height,
[238](#238)            depth_or_array_layers: 1,
[239](#239)        });
[240](#240)        image.data = Some(context.backend().get_pixmap_data_as_rgba());
[241](#241)        return;
[242](#242)    }
[243](#243)
[244](#244)    let data_in = context.backend().get_pixmap_data();
[245](#245)    let data_out = image.data.as_mut().expect("image data missing");
[246](#246)    let (pixels_in, _) = data_in.as_chunks::<3>();
[247](#247)    let (pixels_out, _) = data_out.as_chunks_mut::<4>();
[248](#248)    for (px_in, px_out) in pixels_in.iter().zip(pixels_out.iter_mut()) {
[249](#249)        px_out[0] = px_in[0];
[250](#250)        px_out[1] = px_in[1];
[251](#251)        px_out[2] = px_in[2];
[252](#252)        px_out[3] = 255;
[253](#253)    }
[254](#254)}

[256](#256)fn handle_monitor_pointer_input(
[257](#257)    window: Single<&Window, With<PrimaryWindow>>,
[258](#258)    mouse_buttons: Res<ButtonInput<MouseButton>>,
[259](#259)    context: Res<CuBevyMonTerminal>,
[260](#260)    mut ui_state: ResMut<CuBevyMonUiState>,
[261](#261)    panels: Query<(&ComputedNode, &bevy::ui::UiGlobalTransform), With<CuBevyMonPanel>>,
[262](#262)) {
[263](#263)    if !mouse_buttons.just_pressed(MouseButton::Left)
[264](#264)        && !mouse_buttons.just_released(MouseButton::Left)
[265](#265)    {
[266](#266)        return;
[267](#267)    }
[268](#268)
[269](#269)    let Some((node, transform)) = panels.iter().next() else {
[270](#270)        return;
[271](#271)    };
[272](#272)    let Some(local_point) = focus::local_cursor_position(&window, node, transform) else {
[273](#273)        return;
[274](#274)    };
[275](#275)
[276](#276)    let char_width = context.backend().char_width.max(1) as f32;
[277](#277)    let char_height = context.backend().char_height.max(1) as f32;
[278](#278)    let col = (local_point.x / char_width).floor().max(0.0) as u16;
[279](#279)    let row = (local_point.y / char_height).floor().max(0.0) as u16;
[280](#280)    let event = if mouse_buttons.just_pressed(MouseButton::Left) {
[281](#281)        MonitorUiEvent::MouseDown { col, row }
[282](#282)    } else {
[283](#283)        MonitorUiEvent::MouseUp { col, row }
[284](#284)    };
[285](#285)    let _ = ui_state.0.handle_event(event);
[286](#286)}
[287](#287)
[288](#288)fn handle_monitor_scroll_input(
[289](#289)    focus: Res<CuBevyMonFocus>,
[290](#290)    mut wheel_events: MessageReader<MouseWheel>,
[291](#291)    mut ui_state: ResMut<CuBevyMonUiState>,
[292](#292)) {
[293](#293)    if focus.0 != CuBevyMonSurface::Monitor {
[294](#294)        return;
[295](#295)    }
[296](#296)
[297](#297)    for event in wheel_events.read() {
[298](#298)        if event.y > 0.0 {
[299](#299)            let _ = ui_state.0.handle_event(MonitorUiEvent::Scroll {
[300](#300)                direction: ScrollDirection::Up,
[301](#301)                steps: 1,
[302](#302)            });
[303](#303)        } else if event.y < 0.0 {
[304](#304)            let _ = ui_state.0.handle_event(MonitorUiEvent::Scroll {
[305](#305)                direction: ScrollDirection::Down,
[306](#306)                steps: 1,
[307](#307)            });
[308](#308)        }
[309](#309)
[310](#310)        if event.x > 0.0 {
[311](#311)            let _ = ui_state.0.handle_event(MonitorUiEvent::Scroll {
[312](#312)                direction: ScrollDirection::Right,
[313](#313)                steps: 5,
[314](#314)            });
[315](#315)        } else if event.x < 0.0 {
[316](#316)            let _ = ui_state.0.handle_event(MonitorUiEvent::Scroll {
[317](#317)                direction: ScrollDirection::Left,
[318](#318)                steps: 5,
[319](#319)            });
[320](#320)        }
[321](#321)    }
[322](#322)}
[323](#323)
[324](#324)fn handle_monitor_keyboard_input(
[325](#325)    focus: Res<CuBevyMonFocus>,
[326](#326)    mut keyboard_inputs: MessageReader<KeyboardInput>,
[327](#327)    mut exit: MessageWriter<AppExit>,
[328](#328)    mut ui_state: ResMut<CuBevyMonUiState>,
[329](#329)) {
[330](#330)    if focus.0 != CuBevyMonSurface::Monitor {
[331](#331)        return;
[332](#332)    }
[333](#333)
[334](#334)    for event in keyboard_inputs.read() {
[335](#335)        if event.state != ButtonState::Pressed {
[336](#336)            continue;
[337](#337)        }
[338](#338)
[339](#339)        if let Some(key) = monitor_navigation_key(event.key_code) {
[340](#340)            dispatch_monitor_event(&mut ui_state.0, &mut exit, MonitorUiEvent::Key(key));
[341](#341)        }
[342](#342)
[343](#343)        if let Some(text) = &event.text {
[344](#344)            for ch in text.chars().filter(|ch| !ch.is_control()) {
[345](#345)                dispatch_monitor_event(
[346](#346)                    &mut ui_state.0,
[347](#347)                    &mut exit,
[348](#348)                    MonitorUiEvent::Key(MonitorUiKey::Char(ch.to_ascii_lowercase())),
[349](#349)                );
[350](#350)            }
[351](#351)        }
[352](#352)    }
[353](#353)}
[354](#354)
[355](#355)fn resize_terminal_to_panel(
[356](#356)    mut context: ResMut<CuBevyMonTerminal>,
[357](#357)    panels: Query<&ComputedNode, With<CuBevyMonPanel>>,
[358](#358)) {
[359](#359)    let Some(panel) = panels.iter().next() else {
[360](#360)        return;
[361](#361)    };
[362](#362)    sync_terminal_to_panel(&mut context, panel.size());
[363](#363)}
[364](#364)
[365](#365)fn dispatch_monitor_event(
[366](#366)    ui_state: &mut MonitorUi,
[367](#367)    exit: &mut MessageWriter<AppExit>,
[368](#368)    event: MonitorUiEvent,
[369](#369)) {
[370](#370)    match ui_state.handle_event(event) {
[371](#371)        MonitorUiAction::QuitRequested => {
[372](#372)            exit.write(AppExit::Success);
[373](#373)        }
[374](#374)        MonitorUiAction::None => {}
[375](#375)        MonitorUiAction::CopyLogSelection(_) => {}
[376](#376)    }
[377](#377)}
[378](#378)
[379](#379)fn monitor_navigation_key(key_code: KeyCode) -> Option<MonitorUiKey> {
[380](#380)    match key_code {
[381](#381)        KeyCode::ArrowLeft => Some(MonitorUiKey::Left),
[382](#382)        KeyCode::ArrowRight => Some(MonitorUiKey::Right),
[383](#383)        KeyCode::ArrowUp => Some(MonitorUiKey::Up),
[384](#384)        KeyCode::ArrowDown => Some(MonitorUiKey::Down),
[385](#385)        _ => None,
[386](#386)    }
[387](#387)}

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cu_bevymon/lib.rs.html#143-174)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Plugin-for-CuBevyMonPlugin)### impl [Plugin](https://docs.rs/bevy_app/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_app/plugin/trait.Plugin.html) for [CuBevyMonPlugin](https://docs.rs/struct.CuBevyMonPlugin.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cu_bevymon/lib.rs.html#143-174)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Plugin-for-CuBevyMonPlugin)

### impl [Plugin](https://docs.rs/bevy_app/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_app/plugin/trait.Plugin.html) for [CuBevyMonPlugin](https://docs.rs/struct.CuBevyMonPlugin.html)

Has the plugin finished its setup? This can be useful for plugins that need something
asynchronous to happen before they can finish their setup, like the initialization of a renderer.
Once the plugin is ready,

[should be called.](https://docs.rs/bevy_app/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_app/plugin/trait.Plugin.html#method.finish)`finish`Runs after all plugins are built and finished, but before the app schedule is executed.
This can be useful if you have some resource that other plugins need during their build step,
but after build you want to remove it and send it to another thread.

# cu-logmon 1.0.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cu-logmon/1.0.0

# CuLogMon

Compact Copper monitor that emits a one-line statistical snapshot every second via the normal `debug!` / `info!` macros.
It is designed to work both on `std` targets and in bare-metal builds that route logging through `defmt`.

## What it prints

- Copperlist index and windowed rate (Hz)
- End-to-end latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99 + max) in microseconds
- The slowest task in the last window (p99) and the time spent logging the previous report

## Usage

```
[]
 = {  = "*",  = true } # disable default-features for no_std
```
In `copperconfig.ron`:

```
monitor: (
    type: "cu_logmon::CuLogMon",
)
```
For bare-metal targets, disable default features and enable `defmt`:

```
 = {  = "*",  = false,  = ["defmt"] }
```
## Example

Run the built-in demo (std targets):

```
```
It simulates a 3-task pipeline at ~10 Hz and prints a one-line stat report every second.

### Full Copper runtime sample

There is also a minimal source->task->sink Copper app wired to `CuLogMon`:

```
```
The runtime uses `copperconfig.ron` in this crate and logs to `logs/logmon_copper_app.copper`.

---

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [capture_](https://docs.rs/fn.capture_live_logs.html)- live_ - logs
- Capture structured log entries emitted while `f`runs.
- [format_](https://docs.rs/fn.format_message_only.html)- message_ - only
- [log](https://docs.rs/fn.log.html)
- Public entry point used in release / no-debug paths.
- [log_](https://docs.rs/fn.log_debug_mode.html)- debug_ - mode
- This version of log is only compiled in debug mode This allows a normal logging framework to be bridged.
- [register_](https://docs.rs/fn.register_live_log_listener.html)- live_ - log_ - listener
- Register a live log listener; subsequent logs invoke `cb`.
- [scoped_](https://docs.rs/fn.scoped_live_log_listener.html)- live_ - log_ - listener
- Register a scoped live log listener and remove it when the returned guard is dropped.
- [structured_](https://docs.rs/fn.structured_log_bytes_total.html)- log_ - bytes_ - total
- Returns the total number of bytes written to the structured log stream.
- [unregister_](https://docs.rs/fn.unregister_live_log_listener.html)- live_ - log_ - listener
- Remove all registered live log listeners. No-op if runtime not initialized.
- [unregister_](https://docs.rs/fn.unregister_live_log_listener_id.html)- live_ - log_ - listener_ - id
- Remove a live log listener by id. No-op if runtime not initialized.

# defmt - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/defmt/^1.0/

## Expand description

A highly efficient logging framework that targets resource-constrained devices, like microcontrollers.

Check out the defmt book at [https://defmt.ferrous-systems.com](https://defmt.ferrous-systems.com) for more
information about how to use it.

[§](https://docs.rs#compatibility)Compatibility

The `defmt` wire format might change between minor versions. Attempting to
read a defmt stream with an incompatible version will result in an error,
and any tool used to process that stream should first check for a symbol
named like `_defmt_version_ = X`, where X indicates the wire format version
in use.

Updating your version of defmt might mean you also have to update your
version of `defmt-print` or `defmt-decoder`.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [assert](https://docs.rs/macro.assert.html)
- Just like the `core::assert!``defmt`is used to log the panic message
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_eq.html)- eq
- Just like the `core::assert_eq!``defmt`is used to log the panic message
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_ne.html)- ne
- Just like the `core::assert_ne!``defmt`is used to log the panic message
- [bitflags](https://docs.rs/macro.bitflags.html)
- Generates a bitflags structure that can be formatted with defmt.
- [dbg](https://docs.rs/macro.dbg.html)
- Just like the `std::dbg!``defmt`is used to log the message at`TRACE`level.
- [debug](https://docs.rs/macro.debug.html)
- Logs data at *debug*level.
- [debug_](https://docs.rs/macro.debug_assert.html)- assert
- Just like the `core::debug_assert!``defmt`is used to log the panic message
- [debug_](https://docs.rs/macro.debug_assert_eq.html)- assert_ - eq
- Just like the `core::debug_assert_eq!``defmt`is used to log the panic message
- [debug_](https://docs.rs/macro.debug_assert_ne.html)- assert_ - ne
- Just like the `core::debug_assert_ne!``defmt`is used to log the panic message
- [error](https://docs.rs/macro.error.html)
- Logs data at *error*level.
- [expect](https://docs.rs/macro.expect.html)
- This is an alias for defmt’s `unwrap`
- [info](https://docs.rs/macro.info.html)
- Logs data at *info*level.
- [intern](https://docs.rs/macro.intern.html)
- Creates an interned string (`Str`
- [panic](https://docs.rs/macro.panic.html)
- Just like the `core::panic!``defmt`is used to log the panic message
- [println](https://docs.rs/macro.println.html)
- Always logs data irrespective of log level.
- [timestamp](https://docs.rs/macro.timestamp.html)
- Defines the global timestamp provider for defmt.
- [todo](https://docs.rs/macro.todo.html)
- Just like the `core::todo!``defmt`is used to log the panic message
- [trace](https://docs.rs/macro.trace.html)
- Logs data at *trace*level.
- [unimplemented](https://docs.rs/macro.unimplemented.html)
- Just like the `core::unimplemented!``defmt`is used to log the panic message
- [unreachable](https://docs.rs/macro.unreachable.html)
- Just like the `core::unreachable!``defmt`is used to log the panic message
- [unwrap](https://docs.rs/macro.unwrap.html)
- Unwraps an `Option`or`Result`, panicking if it is`None`or`Err`.
- [warn](https://docs.rs/macro.warn.html)
- Logs data at *warn*level.
- [write](https://docs.rs/macro.write.html)
- Writes formatted data to a `Formatter`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Debug2](https://docs.rs/struct.Debug2Format.html)- Format
- An “adapter” type to feed `Debug`values into defmt macros, which expect`defmt::Format`values.
- [Display2](https://docs.rs/struct.Display2Format.html)- Format
- An “adapter” type to feed `Display`values into defmt macros, which expect`defmt::Format`values.
- [Encoder](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoder.html)
- Encode raw defmt frames for sending over the wire.
- [Formatter](https://docs.rs/struct.Formatter.html)
- Handle to a defmt logger.
- [Str](https://docs.rs/struct.Str.html)
- An interned string created via `intern!`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [flush](https://docs.rs/fn.flush.html)
- Block until host has read all pending data.

- Defines the global defmt logger.

# spin - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/spin/^0.12/

## Expand description

This crate provides [spin-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinlock) versions of the
primitives in `std::sync`. Because synchronization is done through spinning,
the primitives are suitable for use in `no_std` environments.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

-
`Mutex`,`RwLock`,`Once`/`SyncOnceCell`, and`LazyLock`equivalents
-
Support for `no_std`environments
-
`lock_api`
-
Upgradeable `RwLock`guards
-
Guards can be sent and shared between threads
-
Guard leaking
-
Ticket locks
-
Different strategies for dealing with contention

[§](https://docs.rs#relationship-with-stdsync)Relationship with `std::sync`

While `spin` is not a drop-in replacement for `std::sync` (and
[should not be considered as such](https://matklad.github.io/2020/01/02/spinlocks-considered-harmful.html))
an effort is made to keep this crate reasonably consistent with `std::sync`.

Many of the types defined in this crate have ‘additional capabilities’ when compared to `std::sync`:

-
Because spinning does not depend on the thread-driven model of `std::sync`, guards (`MutexGuard``RwLockReadGuard``RwLockWriteGuard`
-
`RwLockUpgradableGuard``RwLockWriteGuard`
-
Guards support [leaking](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nomicon/leaking.html).
-
`Once``call_once`initializer.
-
`RwLock`

Conversely, the types in this crate do not have some of the features `std::sync` has:

- Locks do not track [panic poisoning](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nomicon/poisoning.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

The crate comes with a few feature flags that you may wish to use.

-
`lock_api`enables support for`lock_api`
-
`ticket_mutex`uses a ticket lock for the implementation of`Mutex`
-
`fair_mutex`enables a fairer implementation of`Mutex`that uses eventual fairness to avoid starvation
-
`std`enables support for thread yielding instead of spinning
-
`portable-atomic`enables usage of the`portable-atomic`crate to support platforms without native atomic operations (Cortex-M0, etc.). See the documentation for the`portable-atomic`crate for more information with some requirements for no-std build:[https://github.com/taiki-e/portable-atomic#optional-features](https://github.com/taiki-e/portable-atomic#optional-features)

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use mutex::`- [MutexGuard](https://docs.rs/mutex/struct.MutexGuard.html);- `mutex`
- `pub use relax::`- [Yield](https://docs.rs/relax/struct.Yield.html);- `std`
- `pub use relax::`- [RelaxStrategy](https://docs.rs/relax/trait.RelaxStrategy.html);
- `pub use relax::`- [Spin](https://docs.rs/relax/struct.Spin.html);
- `pub use rwlock::`- [RwLockReadGuard](https://docs.rs/rwlock/struct.RwLockReadGuard.html);- `rwlock`

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [barrier](https://docs.rs/barrier/index.html)- `barrier`
- Synchronization primitive allowing multiple threads to synchronize the beginning of some computation.
- [lazylock](https://docs.rs/lazylock/index.html)- `lazylock`
- Synchronization primitives for lazy evaluation.
- [lock_](https://docs.rs/lock_api/index.html)- api - `lock_api`
- Spin synchronisation primitives, but compatible with `lock_api`
- [mutex](https://docs.rs/mutex/index.html)- `mutex`
- Locks that have the same behaviour as a mutex.
- [once](https://docs.rs/once/index.html)- `once`
- Synchronization primitives for one-time evaluation.
- [relax](https://docs.rs/relax/index.html)
- Strategies that determine the behaviour of locks when encountering contention.
- [rwlock](https://docs.rs/rwlock/index.html)- `rwlock`
- A lock that provides data access to either one writer or many readers.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Barrier](https://docs.rs/type.Barrier.html)- `barrier`
- A primitive that synchronizes the execution of multiple threads. See `barrier::Barrier`
- [Lazy](https://docs.rs/type.Lazy.html)- Deprecated - `lazylock`
- A type alias to `LazyLock`
- [Lazy](https://docs.rs/type.LazyLock.html)- Lock - `lazylock`
- A value which is initialized on the first access. See `lazylock::LazyLock`
- [Mutex](https://docs.rs/type.Mutex.html)- `mutex`
- A primitive that synchronizes the execution of multiple threads. See `mutex::Mutex`
- [Once](https://docs.rs/type.Once.html)- `once`
- A primitive that provides lazy one-time initialization. See `once::Once`
- [RwLock](https://docs.rs/type.RwLock.html)- `rwlock`
- A lock that provides data access to either one writer or many readers. See `rwlock::RwLock`
- [RwLock](https://docs.rs/type.RwLockUpgradableGuard.html)- Upgradable - Guard - `rwlock`
- A guard that provides immutable data access but can be upgraded to `RwLockWriteGuard``rwlock::RwLockUpgradableGuard`
- [RwLock](https://docs.rs/type.RwLockWriteGuard.html)- Write - Guard - `rwlock`
- A guard that provides mutable data access. See `rwlock::RwLockWriteGuard`

# cu_logmon - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cu-logmon/1.0.0/target-redirect/cu_logmon/

## Expand description

Lightweight Copper monitor that periodically dumps compact runtime stats over the
standard `debug!` / `info!` logging macros.

This monitor is `no_std` friendly and keeps allocations to a minimum while still
reporting a per-second summary of the Copperlist cadence and latencies.

---

[150](#150)    fn compute_snapshot(&self, state: &WindowState, now: CuTime) -> Option<Snapshot> {
[151](#151)        let last_report = state.last_report_at?;
[152](#152)
[153](#153)        let elapsed = now - last_report;
[154](#154)        let elapsed_ns = elapsed.as_nanos();
[155](#155)
[156](#156)        if elapsed_ns < CuDuration::from_secs(REPORT_INTERVAL_SECS).as_nanos() {
[157](#157)            return None;
[158](#158)        }
[159](#159)
[160](#160)        let rate_x10 = (state.window_copperlists as u64 * 10 * 1_000_000_000u64)
[161](#161)            .checked_div(elapsed_ns)
[162](#162)            .unwrap_or(0);
[163](#163)
[164](#164)        let top4_max_entries = find_top_components_by_max(&state.per_component, 4);
[165](#165)        let mut top4 = String::new();
[166](#166)        if top4_max_entries.is_empty() {
[167](#167)            top4.push_str("none");
[168](#168)        } else {
[169](#169)            for (rank, (component_id, dur)) in top4_max_entries.iter().enumerate() {
[170](#170)                if rank > 0 {
[171](#171)                    top4.push_str(", ");
[172](#172)                }
[173](#173)                let name = self.component_name(*component_id);
[174](#174)                let _ = write!(&mut top4, "{} {}us", name, dur.as_micros());
[175](#175)            }
[176](#176)        }
[177](#177)
[178](#178)        let e2e_p50 = state.end_to_end.percentile(0.5).as_micros();
[179](#179)        let e2e_p90 = state.end_to_end.percentile(0.9).as_micros();
[180](#180)        let e2e_p99 = state.end_to_end.percentile(0.99).as_micros();
[181](#181)        let e2e_max = state.end_to_end.max().as_micros().max(e2e_p99);
[183](#183)
[184](#184)        Some(Snapshot {
[185](#185)            copperlist_index: state.total_copperlists,
[186](#186)            rate_whole: rate_x10 / 10,
[187](#187)            rate_tenths: rate_x10 % 10,
[188](#188)            e2e_p50_us: e2e_p50,
[189](#189)            e2e_p90_us: e2e_p90,
[190](#190)            e2e_p99_us: e2e_p99,
[191](#191)            e2e_max_us: e2e_max,
[192](#192)            top4,
[193](#193)            overhead_us: state.last_log_duration.as_micros(),
[194](#194)        })
[195](#195)    }

[204](#204)fn end_to_end_latency(msgs: &[&CuMsgMetadata]) -> Option<CuDuration> {
[205](#205)    let start = msgs
[206](#206)        .first()
[207](#207)        .and_then(|m| Option::<CuTime>::from(m.process_time.start));
[208](#208)    let end = msgs
[209](#209)        .last()
[210](#210)        .and_then(|m| Option::<CuTime>::from(m.process_time.end));
[211](#211)    match (start, end) {
[212](#212)        (Some(s), Some(e)) if e >= s => Some(e - s),
[213](#213)        _ => None,
[214](#214)    }

[216](#216)
[217](#217)fn find_top_components_by_max(
[218](#218)    per_component: &[CuDurationStatistics],
[219](#219)    limit: usize,
[220](#220)) -> Vec<(ComponentId, CuDuration)> {
[221](#221)    let mut ranked: Vec<(ComponentId, CuDuration)> = per_component
[222](#222)        .iter()
[223](#223)        .enumerate()
[224](#224)        .filter_map(|(idx, stats)| {
[225](#225)            (!stats.is_empty()).then_some((ComponentId::new(idx), stats.max()))
[226](#226)        })
[227](#227)        .collect();
[228](#228)    ranked.sort_unstable_by(|a, b| {
[229](#229)        b.1.as_nanos()
[230](#230)            .cmp(&a.1.as_nanos())
[231](#231)            .then_with(|| a.0.index().cmp(&b.0.index()))
[232](#232)    });
[233](#233)    ranked.truncate(limit);
[234](#234)    ranked
[235](#235)}

[264](#264)    fn start(&mut self, ctx: &CuContext) -> CuResult<()> {

[266](#266)        window.last_report_at = Some(ctx.recent());
[267](#267)        info!(
[268](#268)            ctx,

[270](#270)        );
[271](#271)
[272](#272)        #[cfg(all(feature = "std", debug_assertions))]
[274](#274)        register_live_log_listener(|entry, format_str, param_names| {
[275](#275)            const PARAM_COLOR: &str = "\x1b[36m"; const RESET: &str = "\x1b[0m";
[277](#277)
[278](#278)            let params: Vec<String> = entry.params.iter().map(|v| v.to_string()).collect();
[279](#279)            let colored_params: Vec<String> = params
[280](#280)                .iter()
[281](#281)                .map(|v| format!("{PARAM_COLOR}{v}{RESET}"))
[282](#282)                .collect();
[283](#283)            let colored_named: HashMap<String, String> = param_names
[284](#284)                .iter()
[285](#285)                .zip(params.iter())
[286](#286)                .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), format!("{PARAM_COLOR}{v}{RESET}")))
[287](#287)                .collect();
[288](#288)
[289](#289)            if let Ok(msg) =
[290](#290)                format_message_only(format_str, colored_params.as_slice(), &colored_named)
[291](#291)            {
[292](#292)                let level_color = match entry.level {
[293](#293)                    CuLogLevel::Debug => "\x1b[32m",   CuLogLevel::Info => "\x1b[90m",    CuLogLevel::Warning => "\x1b[93m", CuLogLevel::Error => "\x1b[91m",   CuLogLevel::Critical => "\x1b[91m",
[298](#298)                };
[299](#299)                let ts_color = "\x1b[34m";
[300](#300)                let ts = format_timestamp(entry.time);
[301](#301)                println!(
[302](#302)                    "{ts_color}{ts}{reset} {level_color}[{:?}]{reset} {msg}",
[303](#303)                    entry.level,
[304](#304)                    ts = ts,
[305](#305)                    ts_color = ts_color,
[306](#306)                    level_color = level_color,
[307](#307)                    reset = RESET,
[308](#308)                    msg = msg
[309](#309)                );
[310](#310)            }
[311](#311)        });
[312](#312)        Ok(())
[313](#313)    }
[314](#314)
[315](#315)    fn process_copperlist(&self, ctx: &CuContext, view: CopperListView<'_>) -> CuResult<()> {
[316](#316)        let call_start = ctx.recent();
[317](#317)
[318](#318)        let snapshot = {
[319](#319)            let mut window = lock_window(&self.window);
[320](#320)            window.last_report_at.get_or_insert(call_start);
[321](#321)
[322](#322)            window.total_copperlists = window.total_copperlists.saturating_add(1);
[323](#323)            window.window_copperlists = window.window_copperlists.saturating_add(1);
[324](#324)
[325](#325)            if let Some(latency) = end_to_end_latency(view.msgs()) {
[326](#326)                window.end_to_end.record(latency);
[327](#327)            }
[328](#328)
[329](#329)            for entry in view.entries() {
[330](#330)                let component_index = entry.component_id.index();
[331](#331)                if let Some(component_stat) = window.per_component.get_mut(component_index)
[332](#332)                    && let Some(duration) = component_duration(entry.msg)
[333](#333)                {
[334](#334)                    component_stat.record(duration);
[335](#335)                } else {
[336](#336)                    debug_assert!(
[337](#337)                        component_index < window.per_component.len(),
[338](#338)                        "cu_logmon: component index {} out of bounds {}",
[339](#339)                        component_index,
[340](#340)                        window.per_component.len()
[341](#341)                    );
[342](#342)                }
[343](#343)            }
[344](#344)
[345](#345)            let snapshot = self.compute_snapshot(&window, call_start);
[346](#346)            if snapshot.is_some() {
[347](#347)                window.reset_window(call_start);
[348](#348)            }
[349](#349)            snapshot
[350](#350)        };
[351](#351)
[352](#352)        if let Some(snapshot) = snapshot {
[353](#353)            let log_start = ctx.recent();
[354](#354)            let use_color = cfg!(feature = "color_log");
[355](#355)            let base = format!(
[356](#356)                "[CL {}] rate {}.{} Hz | top4 {} | e2e p50 {}us p90 {}us p99 {}us max {}us | overhead {}us",
[357](#357)                snapshot.copperlist_index,
[358](#358)                snapshot.rate_whole,
[359](#359)                snapshot.rate_tenths,
[360](#360)                snapshot.top4,
[361](#361)                snapshot.e2e_p50_us,
[362](#362)                snapshot.e2e_p90_us,
[363](#363)                snapshot.e2e_p99_us,
[364](#364)                snapshot.e2e_max_us,
[365](#365)                snapshot.overhead_us,
[366](#366)            );
[367](#367)            if use_color {
[368](#368)                const CL_COLOR: &str = "\x1b[94m"; const LABEL_COLOR: &str = "\x1b[92m"; const SUBLABEL_COLOR: &str = "\x1b[93m"; const COMPONENT_NAME_COLOR: &str = "\x1b[38;5;208m"; const RESET: &str = "\x1b[0m";
[374](#374)                let colored = format!(
[375](#375)                    "[{cl_color}CL {cl}{reset}] {label}rate{reset} {rate_whole}.{rate_tenths} Hz | {label}top4{reset} {component_color}{top4}{reset} | {label}e2e{reset} {sublabel}p50{reset} {p50}us {sublabel}p90{reset} {p90}us {sublabel}p99{reset} {p99}us {sublabel}max{reset} {max}us | {label}overhead{reset} {overhead}us",
[376](#376)                    cl_color = CL_COLOR,
[377](#377)                    label = LABEL_COLOR,
[378](#378)                    sublabel = SUBLABEL_COLOR,
[379](#379)                    component_color = COMPONENT_NAME_COLOR,
[380](#380)                    reset = RESET,
[381](#381)                    cl = snapshot.copperlist_index,
[382](#382)                    rate_whole = snapshot.rate_whole,
[383](#383)                    rate_tenths = snapshot.rate_tenths,
[384](#384)                    p50 = snapshot.e2e_p50_us,
[385](#385)                    p90 = snapshot.e2e_p90_us,
[386](#386)                    p99 = snapshot.e2e_p99_us,

[389](#389)                    overhead = snapshot.overhead_us,
[390](#390)                );
[391](#391)                info!(ctx, "{}", &colored);
[392](#392)            } else {
[393](#393)                info!(ctx, "{}", &base);
[394](#394)            }
[395](#395)            let log_end = ctx.recent();
[396](#396)            lock_window(&self.window).last_log_duration = log_end - log_start;
[397](#397)        }
[398](#398)
[399](#399)        Ok(())
[400](#400)    }
[401](#401)
[402](#402)    fn process_error(
[403](#403)        &self,

[416](#416)    }

# glam - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/glam/^0.30.10/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#glam)glam

`glam` is a simple and fast linear algebra library for games and graphics.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- `f32`
- `f64`
- `i8`
- `u8`
- `i16`
- `u16`
- `i32`
- `u32`
- `i64`
- `u64`
- `usize`
- `bool`

[§](https://docs.rs#simd)SIMD

`glam` is built with SIMD in mind. Many `f32` types use 128-bit SIMD vector types for storage
and/or implementation. The use of SIMD generally enables better performance than using primitive
numeric types such as `f32`.

Some `glam` types use SIMD for storage meaning they are 16 byte aligned, these types include
`Mat2`, `Mat3A`, `Mat4`, `Quat`, `Vec3A`, `Vec4`, `Affine2` an `Affine3A`. Types
with an `A` suffix are a SIMD alternative to a scalar type, e.g. `Vec3` uses `f32` storage and
`Vec3A` uses SIMD storage.

When SIMD is not available on the target the types will maintain 16 byte alignment and internal padding so that object sizes and layouts will not change between architectures. There are scalar math fallback implementations exist when SIMD is not available. It is intended to add support for other SIMD architectures once they appear in stable Rust.

Currently only SSE2 on x86/x86_64, NEON on Aarch64, and simd128 on WASM are supported.

[§](https://docs.rs#vec3a-and-mat3a)Vec3A and Mat3A

`Vec3A` is a SIMD optimized version of the `Vec3` type, which due to 16 byte alignment results
in `Vec3A` containing 4 bytes of padding making it 16 bytes in size in total. `Mat3A` is composed
of three `Vec3A` columns.

Despite this wasted space the SIMD implementations tend to outperform `f32` implementations in
[ mathbench](https://github.com/bitshifter/mathbench-rs) benchmarks.

`glam` treats [ Vec3](https://docs.rs/f32/struct.Vec3.html) as the default 3D vector type and

[a special case for optimization. When methods need to return a 3D vector they will generally return](https://docs.rs/f32/struct.Vec3A.html)

`Vec3A`[.](https://docs.rs/f32/struct.Vec3.html)

`Vec3`There are [ From](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html) trait implementations for converting from

[to a](https://docs.rs/f32/struct.Vec4.html)

`Vec4`[and between](https://docs.rs/f32/struct.Vec3A.html)

`Vec3A`[and](https://docs.rs/f32/struct.Vec3.html)

`Vec3`[(and vice versa).](https://docs.rs/f32/struct.Vec3A.html)

`Vec3A````
use glam::{Vec3, Vec3A, Vec4};
let v4 = Vec4::new(1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0);
// Convert from `Vec4` to `Vec3A`, this is a no-op if SIMD is supported.
// We use an explicit method here instead of a From impl as data is lost in the conversion.
let v3a = Vec3A::from_vec4(v4);
assert_eq!(Vec3A::new(1.0, 2.0, 3.0), v3a);
// Convert from `Vec3A` to `Vec3`.
let v3 = Vec3::from(v3a);
assert_eq!(Vec3::new(1.0, 2.0, 3.0), v3);
// Convert from `Vec3` to `Vec3A`.
let v3a = Vec3A::from(v3);
assert_eq!(Vec3A::new(1.0, 2.0, 3.0), v3a);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#affine2-and-affine3a)Affine2 and Affine3A

`Affine2` and `Affine3A` are composed of a linear transform matrix and a vector translation. The
represent 2D and 3D affine transformations which are commonly used in games.

The table below shows the performance advantage of `Affine2` over `Mat3A` and `Mat3A` over `Mat3`.

| operation | `Mat3` | `Mat3A` | `Affine2` |
|---|---|---|---|
| inverse | 11.4±0.09ns | 7.1±0.09ns | 5.4±0.06ns |
| mul self | 10.5±0.04ns | 5.2±0.05ns | 4.0±0.05ns |
| transform point2 | 2.7±0.02ns | 2.7±0.03ns | 2.8±0.04ns |
| transform vector2 | 2.6±0.01ns | 2.6±0.03ns | 2.3±0.02ns |

Performance is much closer between `Mat4` and `Affine3A` with the affine type being faster to
invert.

| operation | `Mat4` | `Affine3A` |
|---|---|---|
| inverse | 15.9±0.11ns | 10.8±0.06ns |
| mul self | 7.3±0.05ns | 7.0±0.06ns |
| transform point3 | 3.6±0.02ns | 4.3±0.04ns |
| transform point3a | 3.0±0.02ns | 3.0±0.04ns |
| transform vector3 | 4.1±0.02ns | 3.9±0.04ns |
| transform vector3a | 2.8±0.02ns | 2.8±0.02ns |

Benchmarks were taken on an Intel Core i7-4710HQ.

[§](https://docs.rs#linear-algebra-conventions)Linear algebra conventions

`glam` interprets vectors as column matrices (also known as column vectors) meaning when
transforming a vector with a matrix the matrix goes on the left.

```
use glam::{Mat3, Vec3};
let m = Mat3::IDENTITY;
let x = Vec3::X;
let v = m * x;
assert_eq!(v, x);
```
Matrices are stored in memory in column-major order.

All angles are in radians. Rust provides the `f32::to_radians()` and `f64::to_radians()` methods to
convert from degrees.

[§](https://docs.rs#direct-element-access)Direct element access

Because some types may internally be implemented using SIMD types, direct access to vector elements
is supported by implementing the [ Deref](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.Deref.html) and

[traits.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.DerefMut.html)

`DerefMut````
use glam::Vec3A;
let mut v = Vec3A::new(1.0, 2.0, 3.0);
assert_eq!(3.0, v.z);
v.z += 1.0;
assert_eq!(4.0, v.z);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#glam-assertions)glam assertions

`glam` does not enforce validity checks on method parameters at runtime. For example methods that
require normalized vectors as input such as `Quat::from_axis_angle(axis, angle)` will not check
that axis is a valid normalized vector. To help catch unintended misuse of `glam` the
`debug-glam-assert` or `glam-assert` features can be enabled to add checks ensure that inputs to
are valid.

[§](https://docs.rs#vector-swizzles)Vector swizzles

`glam` vector types have functions allowing elements of vectors to be reordered, this includes
creating a vector of a different size from the vectors elements.

The swizzle functions are implemented using traits to add them to each vector type. This is
primarily because there are a lot of swizzle functions which can obfuscate the other vector
functions in documentation and so on. The traits are [ Vec2Swizzles](https://docs.rs/swizzles/trait.Vec2Swizzles.html),

[and](https://docs.rs/swizzles/trait.Vec3Swizzles.html)

`Vec3Swizzles`[.](https://docs.rs/swizzles/trait.Vec4Swizzles.html)

`Vec4Swizzles`Note that the [ Vec3Swizzles](https://docs.rs/swizzles/trait.Vec3Swizzles.html) implementation for

[will return a](https://docs.rs/f32/struct.Vec3A.html)

`Vec3A`[for 3 element swizzles, all other implementations will return](https://docs.rs/f32/struct.Vec3A.html)

`Vec3A`[.](https://docs.rs/f32/struct.Vec3.html)

`Vec3````
use glam::{swizzles::*, Vec2, Vec3, Vec3A, Vec4};
let v = Vec4::new(1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0);
// Reverse elements of `v`, if SIMD is supported this will use a vector shuffle.
let wzyx = v.wzyx();
assert_eq!(Vec4::new(4.0, 3.0, 2.0, 1.0), wzyx);
// Swizzle the yzw elements of `v` into a `Vec3`
let yzw = v.yzw();
assert_eq!(Vec3::new(2.0, 3.0, 4.0), yzw);
// To swizzle a `Vec4` into a `Vec3A` swizzle the `Vec4` first then convert to
// `Vec3A`. If SIMD is supported this will use a vector shuffle. The last
// element of the shuffled `Vec4` is ignored by the `Vec3A`.
let yzw = Vec3A::from_vec4(v.yzwx());
assert_eq!(Vec3A::new(2.0, 3.0, 4.0), yzw);
// You can swizzle from a `Vec4` to a `Vec2`
let xy = v.xy();
assert_eq!(Vec2::new(1.0, 2.0), xy);
// And back again
let yyxx = xy.yyxx();
assert_eq!(Vec4::new(2.0, 2.0, 1.0, 1.0), yyxx);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#simd-and-scalar-consistency)SIMD and scalar consistency

`glam` types implement `serde` `Serialize` and `Deserialize` traits to ensure
that they will serialize and deserialize exactly the same whether or not
SIMD support is being used.

The SIMD versions implement the `core::fmt::Debug` and `core::fmt::Display`
traits so they print the same as the scalar version.

```
use glam::Vec4;
let a = Vec4::new(1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0);
assert_eq!(format!("{}", a), "[1, 2, 3, 4]");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

All `glam` dependencies are optional, however some are required for tests
and benchmarks.

- `approx`- traits and macros for approximate float comparisons
- `arbitrary`- implementations of- `Arbitrary`trait for all- `glam`types.
- `bytemuck`- for casting into slices of bytes
- `encase`-- `encase`trait implementations for- `glam`types.
- `libm`- uses- `libm`math functions instead of- `std`
- `mint`- for interoperating with other 3D math libraries
- `rand`- implementations of- `Distribution`trait for all- `glam`types.
- `rkyv`- implementations of- `Archive`,- `Serialize`and- `Deserialize`for all- `glam`types. Note that serialization is not interoperable with and without the- `scalar-math`feature. It should work between all other builds of- `glam`. Endian conversion is currently not supported
- `bytecheck`- to perform archive validation when using the- `rkyv`feature
- `serde`- implementations of- `Serialize`and- `Deserialize`for all- `glam`types. Note that serialization should work between builds of- `glam`with and without SIMD enabled
- `speedy`- implementations of- `speedy`’s- `Readable`and- `Writable`for all- `glam`types.
- `zerocopy`- implementations of zerocopy traits for safe transmutes.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-gates)Feature gates

- `std`- the default feature, has no dependencies.
- `nostd-libm`- uses- `libm`math functions if- `std`is not available
- `scalar-math`- disables SIMD support and uses native alignment for all types.
- `debug-glam-assert`- adds assertions in debug builds which check the validity of parameters passed to- `glam`to help catch runtime errors.
- `glam-assert`- adds assertions to all builds which check the validity of parameters passed to- `glam`to help catch runtime errors.
- `cuda`- forces- `glam`types to match expected cuda alignment
- `fast-math`- By default, glam attempts to provide bit-for-bit identical results on all platforms. Using this feature will enable platform specific optimizations that may not be identical to other platforms.- **Intermediate libraries should not use this feature and defer the decision to the final binary build**.
- `core-simd`- enables SIMD support via the portable simd module. This is an unstable feature which requires a nightly Rust toolchain and- `std`support.

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version-msrv)Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)

The minimum supported Rust version is `1.68.2`.

# re_log - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/re_log/=0.34.0-rc.4/

## Expand description

Text logging (nothing to do with rerun logging) for use in rerun libraries.

Provides helpers for adding multiple loggers, and for setting up logging on native and on web.

- `trace`: spammy things
- `debug`: things that might be useful when debugging
- `info`: things that we want to show to users
- `warn`: problems that we can recover from
- `error`: problems that lead to loss of functionality or data

The `warn_once` etc macros are for when you want to suppress repeated
logging of the exact same message.

In the viewer these logs, if >= info, become notifications. See
`re_ui::notifications` for more information.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [external](https://docs.rs/external/index.html)
- Re-exports of other crates.

# gilrs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gilrs/^0.11.1/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#gilrs---game-input-library-for-rust)GilRs - Game Input Library for Rust

GilRs abstract platform specific APIs to provide unified interfaces for working with gamepads.

Main features:

- Unified gamepad layout—buttons and axes are represented by familiar names
- Support for SDL2 mappings including `SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG`environment variable which Steam uses
- Hotplugging—GilRs will try to assign new IDs for new gamepads and reuse the same ID for gamepads which reconnected
- Force feedback (rumble)
- Power information (is gamepad wired, current battery status)

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use gilrs::{Gilrs, Button, Event};
let mut gilrs = Gilrs::new().unwrap();
// Iterate over all connected gamepads
for (_id, gamepad) in gilrs.gamepads() {
    println!("{} is {:?}", gamepad.name(), gamepad.power_info());
}
let mut active_gamepad = None;
loop {
    // Examine new events
    while let Some(Event { id, event, time, .. }) = gilrs.next_event() {
        println!("{:?} New event from {}: {:?}", time, id, event);
        active_gamepad = Some(id);
    }
    // You can also use cached gamepad state
    if let Some(gamepad) = active_gamepad.map(|id| gilrs.gamepad(id)) {
        if gamepad.is_pressed(Button::South) {
            println!("Button South is pressed (XBox - A, PS - X)");
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#supported-features)Supported features

| Input | Hotplugging | Force feedback | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux/BSD (evdev) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Windows | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| OS X | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Wasm | ✓ | ✓ | n/a |
| Android | ✕ | ✕ | ✕ |

[§](https://docs.rs#controller-layout)Controller layout

[§](https://docs.rs#mappings)Mappings

GilRs use SDL-compatible controller mappings to fix on Linux legacy drivers that doesn’t follow
[Linux Gamepad API](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/input/gamepad.txt) and to provide
unified button layout for platforms that doesn’t make any guarantees about it. The main source
is [SDL_GameControllerDB](https://github.com/gabomdq/SDL_GameControllerDB), but library also
support loading mappings from environment variable `SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG` (which Steam
use).

[§](https://docs.rs#cargo-features)Cargo features

- `serde-serialize`- enable deriving of serde’s- `Serialize`and- `Deserialize`for various types.
- `wgi`- use Windows Gaming Input on Windows (enabled by default).
- `xinput`- use XInput on Windows.

[§](https://docs.rs#platform-specific-notes)Platform specific notes

[§](https://docs.rs#linuxbsd-evdev)Linux/BSD (evdev)

With evdev, GilRs read (and write, in case of force feedback) directly from appropriate
`/dev/input/event*` file. This mean that user have to have read and write access to this file.
On most distros it shouldn’t be a problem, but if it is, you will have to create udev rule.
On FreeBSD generic HID gamepads use hgame(4) and special use Linux driver via `webcamd`.

To build GilRs, you will need pkg-config and libudev .pc file. On some distributions this file
is packaged in separate archive (e.g., `libudev-dev` in Debian, `libudev-devd` in FreeBSD).

[§](https://docs.rs#windows)Windows

Windows defaults to using Windows Gaming Input instead of XInput. If you need to use XInput you
can disable the `wgi` feature (it’s enabled by default) and enable the `xinput` feature.

Windows Gaming Input requires an in focus window to be associated with the process to receive events. You can still switch back to using xInput by turning off default features and enabling the xinput feature.

Note: Some (Older?) devices may still report inputs without a window but this is not the case for all devices so if you are writing a terminal based game, use the xinput feature instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#wasm)Wasm

Wasm implementation uses stdweb, or wasm-bindgen with the wasm-bindgen feature.
For stdweb, you will need [cargo-web](https://github.com/koute/cargo-web) to build gilrs for
wasm32-unknown-unknown. For wasm-bindgen, you will need the wasm-bindgen cli or a tool like
[wasm-pack](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/installer/).
Unlike other platforms, events are only generated when you call `Gilrs::next_event()`.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::ev::filter::`- [Filter](https://docs.rs/ev/filter/trait.Filter.html);
- `pub use crate::ev::`- [Axis](https://docs.rs/ev/enum.Axis.html);
- `pub use crate::ev::`- [Button](https://docs.rs/ev/enum.Button.html);
- `pub use crate::ev::`- [Event](https://docs.rs/ev/struct.Event.html);
- `pub use crate::ev::`- [EventType](https://docs.rs/ev/enum.EventType.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

# parking_lot - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/parking_lot/^0.12.5/

## Expand description

This library provides implementations of `Mutex`, `RwLock`, `Condvar` and
`Once` that are smaller, faster and more flexible than those in the Rust
standard library. It also provides a `ReentrantMutex` type.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use ::`- [lock_api](https://docs.rs/lock_api/0.4.14/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lock_api/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [deadlock](https://docs.rs/deadlock/index.html)
- [Experimental] Deadlock detection

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [ArcMutex](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcMutexGuard.html)- Guard
- An RAII mutex guard returned by the `Arc`locking operations on`Mutex`.
- [ArcReentrant](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcReentrantMutexGuard.html)- Mutex - Guard
- An RAII mutex guard returned by the `Arc`locking operations on`ReentrantMutex`.
- [ArcRw](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcRwLockReadGuard.html)- Lock - Read - Guard
- An RAII rwlock guard returned by the `Arc`locking operations on`RwLock`.
- [ArcRw](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcRwLockUpgradableReadGuard.html)- Lock - Upgradable - Read - Guard
- An RAII rwlock guard returned by the `Arc`locking operations on`RwLock`. This is similar to the`RwLockUpgradableReadGuard`struct, except instead of using a reference to unlock the`RwLock`it uses an`Arc<RwLock>`. This has several advantages, most notably that it has an`'static`lifetime.
- [ArcRw](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcRwLockWriteGuard.html)- Lock - Write - Guard
- An RAII rwlock guard returned by the `Arc`locking operations on`RwLock`. This is similar to the`RwLockWriteGuard`struct, except instead of using a reference to unlock the`RwLock`it uses an`Arc<RwLock>`. This has several advantages, most notably that it has an`'static`lifetime.
- [Condvar](https://docs.rs/struct.Condvar.html)
- A Condition Variable
- [Once](https://docs.rs/struct.Once.html)
- A synchronization primitive which can be used to run a one-time initialization. Useful for one-time initialization for globals, FFI or related functionality.
- [RawFair](https://docs.rs/struct.RawFairMutex.html)- Mutex
- Raw fair mutex type backed by the parking lot.
- [RawMutex](https://docs.rs/struct.RawMutex.html)
- Raw mutex type backed by the parking lot.
- [RawRw](https://docs.rs/struct.RawRwLock.html)- Lock
- Raw reader-writer lock type backed by the parking lot.
- [RawThread](https://docs.rs/struct.RawThreadId.html)- Id
- Implementation of the `GetThreadId`trait for`lock_api::ReentrantMutex`.
- [Wait](https://docs.rs/struct.WaitTimeoutResult.html)- Timeout - Result
- A type indicating whether a timed wait on a condition variable returned due to a time out or not.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Once](https://docs.rs/enum.OnceState.html)- State
- Current state of a `Once`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [const_](https://docs.rs/fn.const_fair_mutex.html)- fair_ - mutex
- Creates a new fair mutex in an unlocked state ready for use.
- [const_](https://docs.rs/fn.const_mutex.html)- mutex
- Creates a new mutex in an unlocked state ready for use.
- [const_](https://docs.rs/fn.const_reentrant_mutex.html)- reentrant_ - mutex
- Creates a new reentrant mutex in an unlocked state ready for use.
- [const_](https://docs.rs/fn.const_rwlock.html)- rwlock
- Creates a new instance of an `RwLock<T>`which is unlocked.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Fair](https://docs.rs/type.FairMutex.html)- Mutex
- A mutual exclusive primitive that is always fair, useful for protecting shared data
- [Fair](https://docs.rs/type.FairMutexGuard.html)- Mutex - Guard
- An RAII implementation of a “scoped lock” of a mutex. When this structure is dropped (falls out of scope), the lock will be unlocked.
- [Mapped](https://docs.rs/type.MappedFairMutexGuard.html)- Fair - Mutex - Guard
- An RAII mutex guard returned by `FairMutexGuard::map`, which can point to a subfield of the protected data.
- [Mapped](https://docs.rs/type.MappedMutexGuard.html)- Mutex - Guard
- An RAII mutex guard returned by `MutexGuard::map`, which can point to a subfield of the protected data.
- [Mapped](https://docs.rs/type.MappedReentrantMutexGuard.html)- Reentrant - Mutex - Guard
- An RAII mutex guard returned by `ReentrantMutexGuard::map`, which can point to a subfield of the protected data.
- [Mapped](https://docs.rs/type.MappedRwLockReadGuard.html)- RwLock - Read - Guard
- An RAII read lock guard returned by `RwLockReadGuard::map`, which can point to a subfield of the protected data.
- [Mapped](https://docs.rs/type.MappedRwLockWriteGuard.html)- RwLock - Write - Guard
- An RAII write lock guard returned by `RwLockWriteGuard::map`, which can point to a subfield of the protected data.
- [Mutex](https://docs.rs/type.Mutex.html)
- A mutual exclusion primitive useful for protecting shared data
- [Mutex](https://docs.rs/type.MutexGuard.html)- Guard
- An RAII implementation of a “scoped lock” of a mutex. When this structure is dropped (falls out of scope), the lock will be unlocked.
- [Reentrant](https://docs.rs/type.ReentrantMutex.html)- Mutex
- A mutex which can be recursively locked by a single thread.
- [Reentrant](https://docs.rs/type.ReentrantMutexGuard.html)- Mutex - Guard
- An RAII implementation of a “scoped lock” of a reentrant mutex. When this structure is dropped (falls out of scope), the lock will be unlocked.
- [RwLock](https://docs.rs/type.RwLock.html)
- A reader-writer lock
- [RwLock](https://docs.rs/type.RwLockReadGuard.html)- Read - Guard
- RAII structure used to release the shared read access of a lock when dropped.
- [RwLock](https://docs.rs/type.RwLockUpgradableReadGuard.html)- Upgradable - Read - Guard
- RAII structure used to release the upgradable read access of a lock when dropped.
- [RwLock](https://docs.rs/type.RwLockWriteGuard.html)- Write - Guard
- RAII structure used to release the exclusive write access of a lock when dropped.

# re_gamepad - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/re_gamepad/0.34.0-rc.4/target-redirect/wasm32-unknown-unknown/re_gamepad/

## Expand description

Gamepad input handling for the Rerun viewer.

The crate keeps device polling separate from view-specific camera behavior.

Its default mapping uses a conventional dual-stick gamepad layout and returns 3D navigation intents in Rerun’s RUB view space.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Gamepad](https://docs.rs/struct.GamepadInput.html)- Input
- Raw, device-independent gamepad input used by the standard mapping.
- [Gamepad](https://docs.rs/struct.GamepadNavigation.html)- Navigation
- Mapped navigation command for a 3D view.
- [Standard](https://docs.rs/struct.StandardGamepadMapping.html)- Gamepad - Mapping
- Standard dual-stick mapping from raw gamepad input to 3D navigation.

# re_gamepad - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/re_gamepad/0.34.0-rc.4/re_gamepad/index.html

## Expand description

Gamepad input handling for the Rerun viewer.

The crate keeps device polling separate from view-specific camera behavior.

Its default mapping uses a conventional dual-stick gamepad layout and returns 3D navigation intents in Rerun’s RUB view space.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Gamepad](https://docs.rs/struct.GamepadInput.html)- Input
- Raw, device-independent gamepad input used by the standard mapping.
- [Gamepad](https://docs.rs/struct.GamepadManager.html)- Manager
- Native gamepad manager backed by `gilrs`.
- [Gamepad](https://docs.rs/struct.GamepadNavigation.html)- Navigation
- Mapped navigation command for a 3D view.
- [Standard](https://docs.rs/struct.StandardGamepadMapping.html)- Gamepad - Mapping
- Standard dual-stick mapping from raw gamepad input to 3D navigation.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [clear_](https://docs.rs/fn.clear_event_waker.html)- event_ - waker
- Clears the gamepad event callback and parks the backend until it is enabled again.
- [navigation_](https://docs.rs/fn.navigation_from_active_gamepad.html)- from_ - active_ - gamepad
- Polls the active gamepad and maps it to a navigation command.
- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_event_waker.html)- event_ - waker
- Registers a callback that is called whenever the gamepad backend observes input.

[101](#101)impl Default for StandardGamepadMapping {
[102](#102)    fn default() -> Self {
[103](#103)        Self {
[104](#104)            stick_dead_zone: 0.15,
[105](#105)            trigger_dead_zone: 0.05,
[106](#106)            look_speed_radians_per_second: 2.4,
[107](#107)            slow_down_multiplier: 0.25,
[108](#108)            speed_up_multiplier: 4.0,
[109](#109)        }
[110](#110)    }
[111](#111)}
[112](#112)
[113](#113)impl StandardGamepadMapping {
[114](#114)    #[inline]
[116](#116)    pub fn map_input(self, input: GamepadInput, dt: f32) -> GamepadNavigation {
[117](#117)        let left_stick = apply_stick_dead_zone(input.left_stick, self.stick_dead_zone);
[118](#118)        let right_stick = apply_stick_dead_zone(input.right_stick, self.stick_dead_zone);
[119](#119)
[120](#120)        let ascend = apply_trigger_dead_zone(input.right_trigger, self.trigger_dead_zone)
[121](#121)            - apply_trigger_dead_zone(input.left_trigger, self.trigger_dead_zone);
[122](#122)
[123](#123)        let mut local_movement = Vec3::new(left_stick.x, ascend, -left_stick.y);
[124](#124)        if local_movement.length_squared() > 1.0 {
[125](#125)            local_movement = local_movement.normalize_or_zero();
[126](#126)        }
[127](#127)
[128](#128)        let dt = dt.max(0.0);
[129](#129)        let look_delta_radians =
[130](#130)            Vec2::new(right_stick.x, -right_stick.y) * self.look_speed_radians_per_second * dt;
[131](#131)
[132](#132)        let mut speed_multiplier = 1.0;
[133](#133)        if input.slow_down {
[134](#134)            speed_multiplier *= self.slow_down_multiplier;
[135](#135)        }
[136](#136)        if input.speed_up {
[137](#137)            speed_multiplier *= self.speed_up_multiplier;
[138](#138)        }
[139](#139)
[140](#140)        GamepadNavigation {
[141](#141)            local_movement,
[142](#142)            look_delta_radians,
[143](#143)            speed_multiplier,
[144](#144)        }
[145](#145)    }
[146](#146)}
[147](#147)
[148](#148)fn apply_stick_dead_zone(stick: Vec2, dead_zone: f32) -> Vec2 {
[149](#149)    let dead_zone = dead_zone.clamp(0.0, 0.99);
[150](#150)    let length = stick.length();
[151](#151)    if length <= dead_zone {
[152](#152)        Vec2::ZERO
[153](#153)    } else {
[154](#154)        stick * ((length - dead_zone) / (1.0 - dead_zone) / length)
[155](#155)    }
[156](#156)}
[157](#157)
[158](#158)fn apply_trigger_dead_zone(trigger: f32, dead_zone: f32) -> f32 {
[159](#159)    let dead_zone = dead_zone.clamp(0.0, 0.99);
[160](#160)    let trigger = trigger.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
[161](#161)    if trigger <= dead_zone {
[162](#162)        0.0
[163](#163)    } else {
[164](#164)        (trigger - dead_zone) / (1.0 - dead_zone)
[165](#165)    }
[166](#166)}
[167](#167)

## Expand description

Mapped navigation command for a 3D view.

Movement in local RUB view coordinates.

X moves right, Y moves up, and negative Z moves forward.

Look/orbit delta in radians for this frame.

Positive X yaws right. Positive Y pitches down.

Multiplier for translation speed.

Returns true if this navigation command should change the eye.

Performs copy-assignment from

`source`.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/default/trait.Default.html#tymethod.default)

Tests for `self` and `other` values to be equal, and is used by `==`.

Tests for `!=`. The default implementation is almost always sufficient,
and should not be overridden without very good reason.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/borrow/trait.Borrow.html#tymethod.borrow)

# homeboy 0.280.10 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/homeboy/0.280.10

# Homeboy

Homeboy is a component-aware automation CLI for modern software work: many branches, many worktrees, many agents, and many projects moving at once.

It gives local developers, CI jobs, scheduled automation, and coding agents the same operational surface for checks, reviews, tests, benchmarks, traces, releases, and evidence. Humans get readable terminal output; automation gets stable JSON artifacts.

Homeboy core is intentionally domain-agnostic. The CLI owns orchestration, configuration, structured output, persisted runs, baselines, remote execution, and release/evidence workflows. Domain-specific behavior lives in extensions such as Rust, WordPress, Node.js, GitHub, Homebrew, Swift, and custom team extensions.

## What You Can Do

- Run repeatable quality gates with `homeboy audit`,`homeboy lint`,`homeboy test`,`homeboy build`, and`homeboy review`.
- Produce structured evidence with `--output`so CI jobs and coding agents can inspect results without scraping terminal logs.
- Capture benchmark, fuzz, trace, and review artifacts as persisted runs.
- Coordinate many branches and worktrees with comparable checks, reports, and PR evidence.
- Use runners for hot commands, remote execution, and durable agent workflows.
- Plan releases, versions, changelogs, tags, and deploy steps from component metadata.

## Start Here

New to Homeboy? Start with [docs/start-here.md](https://docs.rs/docs/start-here.md). It walks through the first local review gate, the smallest useful `homeboy.json`, JSON evidence, CI, and where each kind of documentation lives.

The shortest useful loop is:

```
```
Portable repo config starts with `homeboy.json`:

```
```
## Common Paths

- [Start here](https://docs.rs/docs/start-here.md)- first-time setup and first successful run.
- [Workflows](https://docs.rs/docs/workflows/index.md)- task guides for reviews, CI reproduction, evidence, runners, agent-task loops, local environments, releases, and fleet operations.
- [Concepts](https://docs.rs/docs/concepts/index.md)- mental models for components, extensions, evidence, runners, and scope.
- [Reference](https://docs.rs/docs/reference/index.md)- command, config, schema, output, and template references.
- [Internals](https://docs.rs/docs/internals/index.md)- maintainer architecture, contracts, and docs-maintenance guidance.
- [Operations](https://docs.rs/docs/operations/index.md)- runbooks for release-gate proof, runner setup, and artifact publication.

# base64 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/base64/^0.22/

## Expand description

Correct, fast, and configurable [base64](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Base64) decoding and encoding. Base64
transports binary data efficiently in contexts where only plain text is
allowed.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Use an [ Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html) to decode or encode base64, configured with the base64
alphabet and padding behavior best suited to your application.

[§](https://docs.rs#engine-setup)Engine setup

There is more than one way to encode a stream of bytes as “base64”.
Different applications use different encoding
[alphabets](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) and
[padding behaviors](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurposeConfig.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#encoding-alphabet)Encoding alphabet

Almost all base64 [alphabets](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) use `A-Z`, `a-z`, and
`0-9`, which gives nearly 64 characters (26 + 26 + 10 = 62), but they differ
in their choice of their final 2.

Most applications use the [standard](https://docs.rs/alphabet/constant.STANDARD.html) alphabet specified
in [RFC 4648](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4648#section-4).  If that’s all you need, you can get started
quickly by using the pre-configured
[ STANDARD](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.STANDARD.html) engine, which is also available
in the

[module as shown here, if you prefer a minimal](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)

`prelude``use`
footprint.```
use base64::prelude::*;
assert_eq!(BASE64_STANDARD.decode(b"+uwgVQA=")?, b"\xFA\xEC\x20\x55\0");
assert_eq!(BASE64_STANDARD.encode(b"\xFF\xEC\x20\x55\0"), "/+wgVQA=");
```
Other common alphabets are available in the [ alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/index.html) module.

[§](https://docs.rs#url-safe-alphabet)URL-safe alphabet

The standard alphabet uses `+` and `/` as its two non-alphanumeric tokens,
which cannot be safely used in URL’s without encoding them as `%2B` and
`%2F`.

To avoid that, some applications use a [“URL-safe” alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/constant.URL_SAFE.html),
which uses `-` and `_` instead. To use that alternative alphabet, use the
[ URL_SAFE](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.URL_SAFE.html) engine. This example doesn’t
use

[to show what a more explicit](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)

`prelude``use` would look like.```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(URL_SAFE.decode(b"-uwgVQA=")?, b"\xFA\xEC\x20\x55\0");
assert_eq!(URL_SAFE.encode(b"\xFF\xEC\x20\x55\0"), "_-wgVQA=");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#padding-characters)Padding characters

Each base64 character represents 6 bits (2⁶ = 64) of the original binary data, and every 3 bytes of input binary data will encode to 4 base64 characters (8 bits × 3 = 6 bits × 4 = 24 bits).

When the input is not an even multiple of 3 bytes in length, [canonical](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4648#section-3.5)
base64 encoders insert padding characters at the end, so that the output
length is always a multiple of 4:

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b""),    "");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"f"),   "Zg==");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"fo"),  "Zm8=");
assert_eq!(STANDARD.encode(b"foo"), "Zm9v");
```
Canonical encoding ensures that base64 encodings will be exactly the same,
byte-for-byte, regardless of input length. But the `=` padding characters
aren’t necessary for decoding, and they may be omitted by using a
[ NO_PAD](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/constant.NO_PAD.html) configuration:

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD_NO_PAD, Engine as _};
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b""),    "");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"f"),   "Zg");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"fo"),  "Zm8");
assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.encode(b"foo"), "Zm9v");
```
The pre-configured `NO_PAD` engines will reject inputs containing padding
`=` characters. To encode without padding and still accept padding while
decoding, create an [engine](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurpose.html) with
that [padding mode](https://docs.rs/engine/enum.DecodePaddingMode.html).

`assert_eq!(STANDARD_NO_PAD.decode(b"Zm8="), Err(base64::DecodeError::InvalidPadding));`[§](https://docs.rs#further-customization)Further customization

Decoding and encoding behavior can be customized by creating an
[engine](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurpose.html) with an [alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html) and
[padding configuration](https://docs.rs/engine/general_purpose/struct.GeneralPurposeConfig.html):

```
use base64::{engine, alphabet, Engine as _};
// bizarro-world base64: +/ as the first symbols instead of the last
let alphabet =
    alphabet::Alphabet::new("+/ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789")
    .unwrap();
// a very weird config that encodes with padding but requires no padding when decoding...?
let crazy_config = engine::GeneralPurposeConfig::new()
    .with_decode_allow_trailing_bits(true)
    .with_encode_padding(true)
    .with_decode_padding_mode(engine::DecodePaddingMode::RequireNone);
let crazy_engine = engine::GeneralPurpose::new(&alphabet, crazy_config);
let encoded = crazy_engine.encode(b"abc 123");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#memory-allocation)Memory allocation

The [decode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.decode) and [encode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.encode) engine methods
allocate memory for their results – `decode` returns a `Vec<u8>` and
`encode` returns a `String`. To instead decode or encode into a buffer that
you allocated, use one of the alternative methods:

[§](https://docs.rs#decoding)Decoding

| Method | Output | Allocates memory |
|---|---|---|
| `Engine::decode` | returns a new `Vec<u8>` | always |
| `Engine::decode_vec` | appends to provided `Vec<u8>` | if `Vec`lacks capacity |
| `Engine::decode_slice` | writes to provided `&[u8]` | never |

[§](https://docs.rs#encoding)Encoding

| Method | Output | Allocates memory |
|---|---|---|
| `Engine::encode` | returns a new `String` | always |
| `Engine::encode_string` | appends to provided `String` | if `String`lacks capacity |
| `Engine::encode_slice` | writes to provided `&[u8]` | never |

[§](https://docs.rs#input-and-output)Input and output

The `base64` crate can [decode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.decode) and
[encode](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html#method.encode) values in memory, or
[ DecoderReader](https://docs.rs/read/struct.DecoderReader.html) and

[provide streaming decoding and encoding for any](https://docs.rs/write/struct.EncoderWriter.html)

`EncoderWriter`[readable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)or

[writable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html)byte stream.

[§](https://docs.rs#decoding-1)Decoding

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, read::DecoderReader};
let mut input = io::stdin();
let mut decoder = DecoderReader::new(&mut input, &STANDARD);
io::copy(&mut decoder, &mut io::stdout())?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#encoding-1)Encoding

```
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, write::EncoderWriter};
let mut output = io::stdout();
let mut encoder = EncoderWriter::new(&mut output, &STANDARD);
io::copy(&mut io::stdin(), &mut encoder)?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#display)Display

If you only need a base64 representation for implementing the
[ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) trait, use

[:](https://docs.rs/display/struct.Base64Display.html)

`Base64Display````
use base64::{display::Base64Display, engine::general_purpose::STANDARD};
let value = Base64Display::new(b"\0\x01\x02\x03", &STANDARD);
assert_eq!("base64: AAECAw==", format!("base64: {}", value));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

If length calculations result in overflowing `usize`, a panic will result.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use engine::`- [Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/index.html)
- Provides [Alphabet](https://docs.rs/alphabet/struct.Alphabet.html)and constants for alphabets commonly used in the wild.
- [display](https://docs.rs/display/index.html)
- Enables base64’d output anywhere you might use a `Display`implementation, like a format string.
- [engine](https://docs.rs/engine/index.html)
- Provides the [Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html)abstraction and out of the box implementations.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Preconfigured engines for common use cases.
- [read](https://docs.rs/read/index.html)
- Implementations of `io::Read`to transparently decode base64.
- [write](https://docs.rs/write/index.html)
- Implementations of `io::Write`to transparently handle base64.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode](https://docs.rs/fn.decode.html)- Deprecated
- Decode base64 using the `STANDARD`engine
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_engine.html)- engine - Deprecated
- Decode from string reference as octets using the specified [Engine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.Engine.html).
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_engine_slice.html)- engine_ - slice - Deprecated
- Decode the input into the provided output slice.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_engine_vec.html)- engine_ - vec - Deprecated
- Decode from string reference as octets.
- [decoded_](https://docs.rs/fn.decoded_len_estimate.html)- len_ - estimate
- Returns a conservative estimate of the decoded size of `encoded_len`base64 symbols (rounded up to the next group of 3 decoded bytes).
- [encode](https://docs.rs/fn.encode.html)- Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 using the `STANDARD`engine
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_engine.html)- engine - Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 using the provided `Engine`into a new`String`.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_engine_slice.html)- engine_ - slice - Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 into a supplied slice.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_engine_string.html)- engine_ - string - Deprecated
- Encode arbitrary octets as base64 into a supplied `String`.
- [encoded_](https://docs.rs/fn.encoded_len.html)- len
- Calculate the base64 encoded length for a given input length, optionally including any appropriate padding bytes.
